range.remark: Pss 66:13-20 (part B), 67, 68, 69, 70-71 (treated as one psalm). Ps 72 begins pdf 54.

entries.note: Before v.13 the portion of this individual psalm that must have contained the thanksgiving proper has evidently been lost; the train of thought — God heard the psalmist's plea, therefore he brings offerings — begins abruptly.

'Incense with rams?' Unintelligible. אילים must denote a land from which spices were imported (cf. Jer 6:20 לבונה משבא); Havilah is a land of gold and spices linked with Sheba and Ophir (Gen 10:29; 2:11-12) — or perhaps אילת, Elath on the Red Sea, where Arabian and Indian wares and spices were unloaded (wares being named after their emporium).
After ואספרה Pesch. has לכון = לכם, out of which כל arose: 'ich will euch, ihr Gottesfürchtigen, erzählen'.
ורומם is correct neither as verb nor as noun; leg. ורוממתו, the תו absorbed by the following תחת — cf. Ps 149:6 רוממות אל.
ראיתי is inexplicable; leg. החבאתי (interchanges of ר/ח and א/ב; cf. Job 31:33 לטמון בחבי עוני): 'Hätte ich ein Vergehen verheimlicht, so würde Gott mein Gebet nicht erhören'.

entries.emendation: move סלה to end of v.3
entries.note: The pause-word סלה in v.2 has strayed to the wrong place and belongs to v.3 (Hupfeld; cf. o. S. 369) — otherwise the text of this psalm is completely correct save one word.
'Lead? Whither?' Leg. תרחם: 'Nationen auf Erden begnadigst Du'.
תנדף is an incongruent form; Pesch. renders both verbs passively — 'wie Rauch verwehet wird, werden sie verweht werden' (interchange in the personal prefixes, o. S. 135).

To let God 'ride through the desert' like a Bedouin only the indestructible per-nefas exegesis could pass; one says רכב שמים and רכב על עב קל. Simply leg. בעבות 'on the clouds' ('den in Wolken Thronenden'). סלו = 'preisen' (Pesch., Targum; Ibn Ezra rightly compares Prov 4:8).
ביה שמו is inexplicable; leg. ברכו שמו, as Ps 96:2 שירו לה' ברכו שמו.
'Einzige' are not 'Vereinzelte', still less 'Arme' or 'Kinderlose'; wohl read a word for fugitives — 'Gott setzte Flüchtlinge in's Haus'.
entries.flag: proposed form garbled in OCR (נדודים?) — verify

entries.note: Out of כושרות nothing else can be made than מוסרות 'bonds' (interchanges of כ/מ and ש/ס): 'führte Gefesselte aus den Banden'.
The perfect would point to an accomplished fact; Pesch. has the future ישכנו 'shall dwell'; צחיחה stands for ארץ צחיחה.

זה fits neither here nor in the original (Judg 5:5, whence vv.8-9 are borrowed); leg. זע 'der Sinai erbebte' (interchange of ה and ע, o. S. 126). In v.9 הרים נזלו of the original appears to have fallen out.
'Regen sprengen' would be little and does not suit נדבות, which must mean 'reichlich'; leg. תטיף 'liessest Du ergiessen' (interchange, o. S. 133).
In what way is the land 'exhausted'? Leg. ומלאה 'sein Erbe und seine Fülle' (Krochmal); the inheritance is the land of Canaan prepared for Israel.

Gives no sense as 'Thiere' or 'Thierchen', as metonym for Israel without analogy, still less as 'Wachtel' (Hupfeld) — the desert is no longer the subject. Leg. מחיתך ישבעו פה (cf. Isa 57:10 חית ידך, leg. מחית ידך); the following relative clause fits excellently: תכין בטובתך, 'von Deinem Nahrungsmittel sättigten sie sich' (cf. Ps 140:14 ישבו leg. ישבעו).
The close לעני is unintelligible; wohl leg. לעם (either עם אלהים or with absorbed article לָעָם, as v.36), and אלהים belongs to the following verse, with תכין as relative (אשר תכין).

entries.emendation: נָתַן אמר הַמְבַשֵּׂר אֶת צבא רב
entries.note: אמר המבשרות is an impossible connection. Leg. המבשר את צבא רב, and statt יתן (which must first be artificially construed as preterite) simply leg. נתן: 'Der Herr gab einen Spruch, so einer grossen Zahl Heilbotschaft bringt'.
ונות בית is inexplicable; leg. וענות — 'die Sanftmüthige des Hauses wird Beute theilen' (the gentle dove being a trope for Israel); שלל also means 'Gewinn' (Ps 119:162).

שפתים = משפתים 'Hürden', as Judg 5:16 (למה ישבת בין המשפתים), so here too leg. שכן statt שכב; the subject can only be the preceding ענות, hence אם תשכן, the ending ־בון dittographed from בין. אם = 'wenn auch': though she rest idle between the sheepfolds, she shall yet have gain — the wings of the gentle dove are covered with silver.

entries.mt: בְּפָרֵשׂ שַׁדַּי מְלָכִים בָּהּ תַּשְׁלֵג בְּצַלְמוֹן
entries.emendation: בפרש שרי מלכי צְבָאוֹת שֶׁלֶג וְצַלְמָוֶת(?)
entries.note: On the received text this is 'zum Verzweifeln', though all old versions had it. Jedenfalls leg. שלג וצלמות (Krochmal; his ברד statt בה lies too far). Since v.12(13) says מלכי צבאות, so probably here too: the undivided letters may be redivided as מלכי צבאת שלג בצלמות. A word is missing — vielleicht ברד, or a verb; in any case a reminiscence of Josh 10:11 (the hailstones on the Canaanite kings). Dyserinck's בהשלחם בצלמות does not commend itself.
entries.flag: letter-details of the redivision garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: For the four-fold הר LXX have thrice הרי, and v.17 has הרים גבננים; so leg. הרי. And statt אלהים leg. אלפים 'Stierberge' (o. S. 346): an apostrophe to the peaks of Bashan — 'Ihr Rinderberge, Berge Baschans'.
Durchaus leg. תרקדון 'why do ye leap' (cf. Ps 29:6 ירקידם ... לבנון and o. S. 197).

שנאן is inexplicable; a Greek variant of LXX points to ישרון, so רבתים אלפי ישורון = רבבות אלפי ישראל (Num 10:36), with רכב as 'Thronwagen' and אלפי as 'clans' (not thousands): 'Gottes Thron zwei Myriaden der Familien Jeschuruns'.

entries.emendation: supply: אדני בם יָרַד עַל סיני בקדשו
entries.note: The half-verse remains difficult unless a word-gap is assumed: supply ירד על — אדני בם (= בתוכם, in their midst) ירד על סיני, and בקדש per Pesch. בקדשה 'in His holiness'; so roughly Targum with homiletic paraphrase.

God taking captives on high and receiving gifts among men? Riddling, though each word is clear. In any case באדם must be emended to בארץ or באדמה (o. S. 198): the subject of עלית can be the people (as v.24), למרום has הרים to be supplied, and the מתנות are the allotted portions (גורלות) of the land God gave the tribes — continuing the narrative of the wandering and the conquest.

Pesch. gives the hold ('and apostates shall not dwell before God'): leg. ואך statt ואף, as v.7b, hence ואך סוררים לא ישכנו בה. The stranded אלהים is probably the fragment of a lost verse — from here a transition to another train of thought follows; LXX draw אלהים to the next verse (κύριος ὁ θεὸς εὐλογητός).

'Der uns auflegt'? Not properly intelligible. Vielleicht עומד לנו 'who stands by us' (Koh 2:9), but that is Neo-Hebrew; Pesch. 'who assigns our inheritance' suggests יעמיד לנו ירושתו statt ישועתנו — which would give good sense, v.21 (האל לנו אל למושעות) being otherwise a tautology.
'Exits, ways of rescue' with למות is unusual; ממות would at least be more logical.
קדקד שער is untenable; leg. רשע (Dyserinck, Krochmal). And מתהלך is not pregnant enough; leg. מתהלל 'so sich seiner Schuld rühmt'.

entries.emendation: מִבֵּין שִׁנַּיִם אשיב, אֲשִׁיבֵם ממצלות ים
entries.note: אשיב מבשן, senseless, should long since have been corrected per Pesch. ('from between the teeth' — so too the talmudic exposition): even if held between the teeth of wild beasts God will draw the people out; and from אשיב ממצלות is to be formed אשיבם — parallel 'aus der Meerestiefe'.
Neither מחץ nor רחץ fits; leg. a form of חמץ 'roth werden' (Krochmal): 'Damit Du röthest Deinen Fuss in Blut' (cf. his identical emendation at Ps 58:11).
מנהו is dark: אחד (Dyserinck) and Krochmal's proposal do not satisfy, nor מלא 'sättigen'; perhaps a short word is to be read with letter-interchanges and the ו struck.
entries.flag: his own proposal garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: Without saying who saw, the verse is unintelligible — a verse seems to be missing. הליכות cannot mean 'Züge/Wege' (in Job 6:19 it is 'caravans', Nah 2:6 simply 'going'); as in Prov 31:27 (where read מלאכות ביתה), leg. מלאכותיך 'Deine Thaten' (= מעשיך, cf. Ps 73:28).
The close is unintelligible; vielleicht leg. 'in Kadesh' (Olshausen's conjecture) — the whole Sinai peninsula, the theatre of the wandering, is called מדבר קדש (Ps 29:8).
Perhaps read the verb (נגנו) after קדמו שרים; and 'the maidens forming the circle around the male singers would be ungallant' — wohl leg. adverbially 'in der Mitte' were the timbrel-striking maidens.
entries.flag: both proposed forms garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: Narrative like the preceding verse, so leg. ברכו as perfect: 'In Chören priesen sie Gott'.
Not properly symmetrical, and ממקור does not fit; Dyserinck's מחוקקי — 'den Gesetzgeber Israels' — is cited in his translation with a query.

entries.mt: בִּנְיָמִן צָעִיר רֹדֵם שָׂרֵי יְהוּדָה רִגְמָתָם
entries.note: רדם is not properly explicable (רדה would mean 'rule', unfitting, and is mostly construed with ב); wohl leg. רדפם 'hat sie verfolgt' (as Isa 14:6, where רדה leg. רדף), and for רגמתם simply רגמום 'sie gesteinigt'. Two southern and two northern tribes are named; little Benjamin shows numbers do not matter. שם points to a historical scene — possibly a verse is missing here too.
entries.flag: form of the second verb garbled in OCR (רגמום?) — verify

entries.note: Per the versions leg. imperative with vocative: 'Entbiete, Gott, Deine Macht'; זו is relative — 'the might Thou hast wrought for us' sums up the historical recollections.
Leg. להיכלך עד (interchange of על and עד, o. S. 127): 'Für Deinen Tempel nach Jerusalem werden Dir Könige Gaben bringen'.
Unintelligible; leg. געלי עמים 'who treat peoples with contempt' (cf. Ezek 16:45 גערה אישה ובניה): 'der Völkerverachtenden'. חית קנה is a figure for Egypt, עדת אבירים the horde of Apis-bulls.
מתרפס = מהתרפס, to wallow (רפס = רפש 'Schlamm'; LXX 'not to wallow'); ברצי כסף is probably transposed and mutilated statt בצברי כסף 'auf Silberhaufen'.
Per the versions read the imperative: 'Zerstreue die Völker, so Kriege lieben!'
חשמנים is inexplicable; leg. משמנים 'Reichbegüterte' (magnates).
Leg. תרים ידיה: 'Aethiopien wird seine Hand zu Gott erheben'.

entries.emendation: draw to v.34 and read לָרֹכֵב
entries.note: סלה is rightly drawn to the following verse and read with לרכב, as v.5 (Hupfeld, Dyserinck).
entries.flag: exact resulting text garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: Leg. במקדשיך: 'Verehrungswürdig ist Gott in Seinem Heiligthum'. At the close, ברוך אלהים leg. with יום יום as v.20.
LXX ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐλπίζειν, i.e. מן + infinitive: 'meine Augen schwinden vom Harren'.
Leg. מצמותי 'than my hair-locks' (Ewald), parallel to שערות ראשי: 'reicher als meine Locken meine Feinde umsonst'.

Völlig sinnlos — one cannot assume the psalmist was accused of robbery and held to restitution; reading it as a proverb is a makeshift. A radical cure: statt גזלתי leg. גמלתי (ז/מ), statt אז leg. אך, statt אשיב leg. טוב (ש/ט): 'denen ich nichts als Gutes vergolten'.
LXX συνέκαμψα: leg. ואענה 'Demüthigte ich meine Seele in Fasten'.
תאטר is a hapax legomenon; leg. a form of אטם 'verschliessen': 'dass der Brunnen nicht über mich seine Oeffnung verschliesse'.
Leg. כטוב, cf. Ps 63:4 and 109:21: 'nach Deiner liebevollen Huld'.
The suffix is unfitting; Pesch. לקבל כלהון — read נגד כל, one letter dittographed: 'in Gegenwart all meiner Feinde'.
entries.flag: exact analysis garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: Leg. לבניהם statt לפניהם (Dyserinck): 'möge ihre Tafelfreude ihren Kindern zum Unglück und ihren Freunden zum Unheil werden' — with a further emendation for לפח.
entries.flag: his reading for לפח garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: תמיד is widersinnig — whoever totters and falls once has enough of it; it need not be constantly repeated. Leg. a form with interchange of ת and מ (o. S. 134).
entries.flag: proposed form garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: טירתם would be a fortified castle, which does not fit; leg. דירתם, Aramaic and Neo-Hebrew 'Wohnung': 'Ihre Wohnung sei verödet'.

entries.mt: כִּי־אַתָּה אֲשֶׁר־הִכִּיתָ רָדָפוּ וְאֶל־מַכְאוֹב חֲלָלֶיךָ יְסַפֵּרוּ
entries.note: Why the emphatic אתה? For יספרו LXX προσέθηκαν and Pesch. have 'they added': leg. ואל מכאוב חלליך יוסיפו, and a. parallel to b.: כי אֹתָם אשר הכית רדפו — 'die, so Du geschlagen, verfolgten sie, und zum Schmerz Deiner Verwundeten thun sie noch hinzu'.
Unintelligible; leg. יראו (interchange of ב and ר, o. S. 190): they shall not see the promised salvation (צדקה) — 'dass sie Dein Heil nicht sehen'.
משור פר is tautology; Pesch. 'a fattened bull' — leg. שור בריא 'feiste Opferstiere', and מקרן leg. ממקרין.
Pesch. renders as imperatives: 'Seht's, ihr Sanftmüthigen, und freut euch'.

Pss 70-71 form one connected piece, Ps 70 being the close of Ps 40. להזכיר in the heading is a mutilation of לבי עזבני (Ps 40:13b); Ps 40:12-13 accordingly belong to Ps 70, which must have contained more verses at its opening.
In v.2 רצה is in any case missing at the head, as the doublet Ps 40:14 shows.
Old manuscripts read outright מעוז statt מעון (Norzi ad loc.); cf. the parallel Ps 31:3-4.
Parallel אתה גחי (Ps 22:10); both are to be read alike ('von Mutterschooss an').
entries.flag: which form he standardizes on garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: תהלתי בך is unfitting; Symmachus ὑπομονή μου, i.e. תוחלתי: 'Auf Dich ist meine Hoffnung beständig'.
Ganz unverständlich; leg. כמו פתי 'wie ein Unbeholfener, Rathloser' — his translation: 'Wie ein Thor bin ich den Fürsten geworden'.
entries.flag: his translation 'den Fürsten' suggests he also emended לרבים (לרוזנים?) — the note is garbled in OCR, verify

entries.note: The י of the verb belongs to the preceding word: leg. עזי, leaving מלא פי תהלתך 'Voll ist mein Mund Deines Lobes'.
Pesch. עלי, which is more correct (cf. S. 238 and Pss 35:19, 39:8, 40:16): 'meine Feinde würden von mir sprechen'.

יבשו יכלו do not fit together; Pesch. נחפרון = יכלמו (the מ having dropped). And שטני נפשי would properly mean 'my accusers' (o. S. 292), of which the psalm knows nothing; leg. שמרי נפשי, as v.10 שמרי נפשי.
איחל fits neither what precedes nor תהלתך in b.; leg. אהלל: 'Ich werde stets loben und vermehren all Deinen Lobpreis'.

Un-Hebrew and not properly intelligible. If the sense is as Ps 40:6 (עצמו מספר), one would have to read the infinitive (referring to צדקה and תשועה), with כי concessive — 'wiewohl ich sie nicht zu zählen wüsste'. But the reading is not assured.
'Ich werde kommen mit der Macht' is geschmacklos; he reads a verb of proclaiming — 'Ich werde verkünden Deine Macht'.
entries.flag: proposed verb garbled in OCR (אשיח? אביע?) — verify at high res

entries.note: לבדך sounds odd; leg. לנגדך: 'werde Deine Gerechtigkeit vor Dir rühmen'.
ועד הנה still belongs to a. (למדתני = 'geleitet', as Isa 40:14); consequently a word is missing in b. before אגיד נפלאותיך.
Joining לדור לכל יבוא (with the versions) is un-Hebrew; the accent-division is right, only לדור means the living generation (like לדור הזה) and must be vocalized as Ps 22:31.

entries.emendation: read the Ketib plurals הִרְאִיתָנוּ, תְּחַיֵּינוּ, תַּעֲלֵנוּ
entries.note: The Ketib is plural throughout (so Aquila and twice Targum): it refers to the whole people's sufferings, surely the Babylonian exile. ומתהומות הארץ seems to designate Babylonia itself — Deutero-Isaiah likewise calls Babylon מצולה (Isa 44:27, where לצולה leg. למצולה): the exiles from the hill-country called the Babylonian lowland 'the deep'; 'Du wirst uns aus dem Tiefland wieder hinausbringen'.

entries.emendation: גְּדֻלָּתְךָ; draw גם אני from v.22 to v.21
entries.note: The verb is precative, and per LXX (ἐμεγάλυνας... σου) read the second person: גדלתך 'Mögest Du Deine Grösse vermehren'. V.21 is moreover exceedingly short and v.22 too long: draw גם אני over — ותסב תנחמני גם אני 'wirst auch mich trösten' (cf. Gen 27:38 ברכני גם אני); תסב means to take another turn, as it were change of mind.
Pesch. renders as future; the י was absorbed (o. S. 139): 'wenn beschämt sein und erröthen werden, so mein Unglück suchen'.
